1001279.etyen:
Borrowed from Middle Low German Jurian, a Low German form of Georg, from Latin Georgius, from Ancient Greek Γεώργιος (Geṓrgios), from Ancient Greek γεωργός (geōrgós, “farmer”), from Ancient Greek γῆ (gê, “earth”) + Ancient Greek ἔργον (érgon, “work”). Doublet of Georg (“male given name”). Attested as a given name in Norway First attested in the 14th century.
Compare Danish Jørgen, Swedish Jörgen, German Jürgen, English George and Norwegian Nynorsk Jørgen (“male given name”).

1004351.etyen:
First attested in 1920 as a newly coined name based on the river name Orkla, with land (“land, territory”) as the second element. The first element ultimately reflects the reconstructed Old Norse river name *Ork, of uncertain origin; it has traditionally been connected with orka (“to work, labour”), perhaps in reference to the river's strong current. The present municipality, established in 2020, reused the historical name.
Compare Orkanger and Orkdal, formed from the same river-name element.

1004863.etyen:
Internationalism, based on the international name stem Vatikan-, ultimately from Latin Vātī̆cānus (“Vatican Hill”), with the Norwegian neuter definite singular ending -et (“definite singular ending”), literally “the Vatican”. The Latin name is of unknown further origin; the connection with vāticinārī (“to prophesy”) is folk-etymological.
Compare the parallel forms Danish Vatikanet, Swedish Vatikanen, German Vatikan, Dutch Vaticaan, Italian Vaticano and English Vatican.

1005119.etyen:
From e (“the note E”) + -iss (“semitone-raising suffix”) + -iss (“semitone-raising suffix”), literally “E-sharp-sharp”. The suffix -iss (“semitone-raising suffix; sharp”) is from German -is (“semitone-raising suffix; sharp”).
Compare the parallel formations Danish eisis, Swedish eississ, German Eisis, Dutch eisis and Finnish eisis (“E double sharp”).
